This screen lets you build and organise every button that appears on your macro pad. Changes are saved immediately — there is no separate save step.
Tap a chip to switch the active profile. The active one is highlighted. Each profile contains its own set of layouts and macros, so you can have separate setups for different games.
Tap the add (+) button next to the Profiles header to create a brand-new empty profile.
Tap the options (three dots) icon to rename, duplicate, reorder, or delete profiles.
A profile can have multiple layouts. Only enabled layouts appear in the Quick Menu for quick switching. Long-press and drag a layout chip to reorder them.
Tap the add (+) button next to the Layouts header to create a new layout inside the current profile.
Tap the options (three dots) icon to rename, duplicate, copy to another profile, or delete layouts.
Places a new macro button on the canvas. After tapping, you can drag it to any position while the canvas is unlocked.
Opens the background image configuration where you can choose or remove a background image, scrape covers from SteamGridDB, crop/scale the image, or toggle mask mode.
Opens the Macros list for this profile, where you can create, edit, and organise reusable macro sequences.
Cycles through grid modes: Off → Rectangular → Radial. When a grid is active, buttons snap to grid positions as you drag them, making precise layouts much easier.
Locking prevents accidental button moves. Tap the lock icon to allow repositioning again.
While the canvas is unlocked, hold and drag any button to reposition it freely. Release to place it.
Tap any button in the list below the canvas to open the Edit dialog. Here you can change its label, icon, size, shape, color, haptics, and assigned macro action.
Drag the handle on the right side of a list item to reorder buttons in the list.
The Macro List shows every reusable macro belonging to the current profile. Macros are independent sequences of input steps that can be assigned to one or more pad buttons.
Creates a new empty macro and opens the Timeline Editor immediately so you can start adding steps. Give it a meaningful name at the top of the editor.
Opens the Macro Timeline Editor for that macro so you can view or edit its steps.
Each macro row has an options menu (three dots) to Rename, Duplicate, Copy to profile, or Delete the macro. Deletion is permanent.
Long-press the drag handle on the right side of a macro row and move it to reorder macros in the list. The order here is cosmetic only and does not affect execution.
The Timeline Editor is where you build the exact sequence of inputs that a macro performs. Steps are executed in order from top to bottom. Timings are recorded precisely or entered manually.
Tap the text field to rename the macro. The name is saved when you tap Save.
Discards all unsaved changes to this macro and returns to the Macro List. Steps you added during this session are lost.
Saves the current name and all steps to the profile. The button is greyed out if the name field is empty.
Reverts the last change to the step list. Up to 50 undo steps are kept during the current editing session.
Re-applies a change that was previously undone. Redo history is cleared whenever you make a new edit.
Shows all steps as a vertical scrollable list — the most readable view for reviewing and editing individual step timings.
Shows steps laid out horizontally on a time axis. Useful for spotting gaps, overlaps, and the overall shape of the macro timing.
Controls how steps coming after the edited step shift: None (no shift), By start delay (shift by start time changes), or By total duration (shift by start time or duration changes).
Opens a picker where you choose the input type: key press, gamepad button, mouse click, scroll, delay, and more.
Records a real tap or gesture on the primary screen and converts it into Touch steps. The mirroring stream is started automatically if it isn\'t active.
Captures live button presses from the physical controller and converts them into Gamepad steps. If Privileged Mode is active, the physical gamepad recorder is used for higher fidelity.
Executes the current macro steps immediately on the device so you can verify the sequence. Loop playback is disabled during test runs.
Tap the edit (pencil) icon or the step row itself to open the configuration dialog for that step.
Tap the delete (trash) icon to remove the step from the macro timeline.
When enabled, the macro repeats continuously until stopped. You can set a pause between repetitions using the slider that appears below the toggle.
Adds a small random offset (±range) to each step\'s timing on every execution. This makes the macro feel less mechanical and can help avoid bot-detection patterns in some apps.
These settings control how the mirrored top-screen image looks in ambient mode — when Megingiard runs in the background behind your buttons. All changes apply to the currently active layout only.
Reduces the brightness of the mirrored image by overlaying a black veil. 0% means no dimming; 90% is nearly black. Use the eye icon to preview the effect live on the secondary screen without saving.
Fades the edges of the mirror image inward so the mirrored content transitions smoothly into the background rather than cutting off sharply. Higher values produce a stronger vignette effect.
Centers the mirrored viewport on the spot you last touched on the primary screen. Select a cutout from the dropdown to enable it, or choose Off to disable.
Lists all mirroring cutouts defined for this layout. You can rename each cutout using its edit (pencil) icon, or adjust its motion smoothing and touch projection settings.
Applies motion smoothing to the cutout panning (Off, Light, Medium, or Strong). Higher values make the viewport movement smoother during panning but can add a tiny amount of latency.
Translates touch inputs on the mirrored cutout area back to the primary display. When active, touches inside the cutout trigger corresponding actions on the main screen.

Activates a live preview of that slider value on the secondary screen. Interact with the secondary screen\'s controls to confirm or cancel the value. This lets you see the effect without navigating away.

The Mirror Editor lets you add, position, resize, and configure the viewport cutouts that appear on the secondary screen during mirroring. Select a cutout by tapping it on screen, then use the toolbar buttons below to act on it.
Creates a new viewport cutout at a free position on the secondary screen. Up to 10 cutouts are allowed per layout. The new cutout is automatically selected.
Opens the per-layout ambient display settings (dim level, edge blending, smoothing). Changes apply only to the currently active layout.

Cycles through three aspect ratio modes for the selected cutout. Free — no constraint, resize independently. Top — lock aspect ratio to match the crop on the Top screen. Bottom — lock aspect ratio to match the cutout on the Bottom screen.
Toggles the selected cutout between rectangle and circle shapes. Useful for game mini-maps or round gauges that look better clipped to a circle.
Opens the crop selector for the selected cutout, letting you drag a frame over the top screen to choose which region is mirrored into this cutout.
Permanently removes the selected cutout from the layout. If the deleted cutout had touch-follow enabled, that mode is also deactivated.
Saves all changes made in this session and closes the editor. The updated cutout layout becomes immediately active.
Discards all changes made since the editor was opened and reverts the layout to its previous state. No modifications are saved.
Global Settings apply to the whole app and persist across sessions. Use the section jump row at the top to scroll quickly to a specific group.
Recommended if your hand grip naturally rests near the bottom of the device, making the Quick Menu easier to swipe open without shifting your thumbs.
Fades out the edge quick menu bar visually after a few seconds. The swipe gestures will still register normally even when the bar is fully invisible, allowing you to open the Quick Menu anytime.
Essential for seamless gaming. Links macro profiles to specific apps so your custom buttons switch instantly when launching a game, without manual menu navigation.
Keeps your Android Recents menu clean. Recommended if you launch Megingiard once and control it entirely via the edge quick menu bar overlay while gaming.
Required for automatic profile switching. Android permissions require this service to detect which game is active on the primary screen. Tap this row to configure.
Changes the language of all app menus, overlays, and help tutorials. Choose English or German depending on your preference.
Enable this if you prefer the Nintendo layout (A on right, B on bottom) over the default Xbox layout (A on bottom, B on right) for gamepad macro actions.
Customizes the highlight color for active buttons and tabs. Note that custom accents do not apply to the Cyberpunk theme, which uses fixed neon styling.
Select Dark or Light theme to customize the app with your chosen accent color, or select Cyberpunk for a styled neon design.
Use this to revert all settings to factory defaults if something gets misconfigured. This will delete all your custom profiles, layouts, and macros.
Creates a complete backup of your custom profiles and configurations. Recommended before performing app updates or resetting settings.
Restores your profiles and configurations from a previously saved .mgrd file or daily automatic backup. Overwrites current configurations upon confirmation.
Saves a single profile to a file to share layout and macros with other players without exposing your entire app configuration.
Adds a shared profile from another user to your collection. This operation is safe and will not modify or overwrite your existing profiles.
Opens Obtainium (if installed) with the pre-filled Megingiard repository link. If Obtainium is not installed, it opens the Obtainium GitHub releases page in the browser.

Establishes a background helper connection via Wireless Debugging to write to system input devices not accessible by regular apps. This enables:

• Gamepad Merge: Combines virtual and physical gamepads so games see only one controller (improving compatibility).
• Physical Gamepad Recording: Record macro inputs from your physical controller.
• Privileged Screen Mirroring: Starts mirroring without prompting for screen capture permissions on every run.
• Screenshots: Save screenshots of the primary screen directly from the Quick Menu overlay without screen mirroring being active.
Ensures analog stick recordings don\'t capture drift or noise. Match these percentages with the dead zone settings in the Thor system settings for best accuracy.
If active, shows a helpful reconnect wizard dialog on app start if the background helper connection drops, allowing you to pair and resume instantly.
Leave at Warn or Info for normal gameplay. Set to Debug or Verbose only when reproducing an issue to gather detailed logs for a bug report.
Exports the latest system logs. Generate this immediately after experiencing a bug or crash to attach it to a GitHub issue or developer report.
Configure layouts and keys for the virtual keyboard.

Select your preferred letters arrangement (QWERTY, QWERTZ, or AZERTY). Note that this configuration only impacts the letters (ABC) keyboard layout mode. Numeric and symbols layout layers remain identical across regional formats.

Show a small relative touchpad in the area above the keyboard layout when the keyboard is open. Gestures like tap-to-click, two-finger tap (right click), and two-finger scroll are supported. Pointer speed and scroll speed sensitivity settings are inherited from the Touchpad Settings menu.

The Quick Menu gives you fast access to profiles, layouts, and the most common actions — all without leaving your current game. Tap the quick menu bar on the screen edge to open it; tap the scrim to close.
Starts or stops the screen mirroring capture. When mirroring is active the top card expands to show additional controls.
Freezes the mirrored image so it shows a still frame instead of the live feed. Useful for pausing a game scene while you read it carefully.
Opens the Cutout Layout Editor on the secondary screen so you can resize, move, or add transparent cutout windows in the mirror overlay.
Takes a screenshot of the main screen. If mirroring is not active, this requires Privileged Mode to be connected.
Tap a chip to instantly switch to a different macro profile. The currently active profile is highlighted. Profiles and their layouts are created and managed in the Edit Profile/Layout screen.
Tap a chip to switch to a different button layout within the current profile. Only layouts marked as enabled in the editor appear here.
Opens the Edit Profile/Layout screen where you can add, move, and configure buttons, manage profiles and layouts, and create or edit macros.
Opens the Global Settings screen for app-wide configuration such as theme, accent color, mirror auto-start, and Privileged Mode setup.
Gracefully closes Megingiard, stopping screen mirroring and background services.
Opens this help sheet with an explanation of every control in the Quick Menu.

Megingiard is a companion app for the AYN Thor dual-screen handheld. It allows you to configure custom MacroPad profiles, virtual keyboard maps, virtual touchpads, and screen mirroring between displays.
Look for the help icon (?) in the top-right corner of each screen to view detailed guides and best practices for that feature.
Reset all tutorial popups to show them again on next access
Tutorials will now be shown again
Forces all tutorial screens and welcome popups to be shown again upon access, even if you previously dismissed them.
Macros allow you to automate sequences of controller inputs or screen taps.
For the best experience, enable Privileged Mode in Global Settings. This allows you to record macros by pressing the physical buttons on your Thor device.
If Privileged Mode is not active, a virtual touch gamepad overlay will be shown on the screen to let you record controller inputs.

You can add steps manually using the toolbar below. When doing so, try to think of the timing you use to actually input the commands yourself in the game: start by mimicking those physical timings and inputs exactly first, and optimize them afterwards (for example, for faster execution). While default timings are automatically added to create a logical sequence, they almost always have to be adapted to the specific needs of the game.

You can enable timing randomization under the Settings section at the bottom of the List view. This adds a slight random offset to step delays on every playback, simulating human inconsistency. This is highly recommended for online games to prevent anti-cheat detection. Please remember that macros are supposed to make your life easier while not making the life of other players harder; the app and this feature are not meant for cheating online.

Swipe the quick menu bar indicator at the edge of the screen to open the Quick Menu. You can use it to switch profiles, layouts, or settings quickly.\n\nNote: You can configure the bar to fade out automatically in Global Settings (Appearance) if you prefer a cleaner look. This behavior is disabled by default.
